
---
title: "Gradients and Directional Derivatives"
---

## The gradient

For a differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\),

$$
\nabla f(x,y)
=
\left\langle f_x(x,y),f_y(x,y)\right\rangle.
$$

The gradient points in the direction of steepest ascent.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Geometric intuition"}

The gradient is perpendicular to the level curve through
the point. It points toward increasing values of the function.

:::

## Example

Let

$$ f(x,y)=x^2+2y^2. $$

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Hint"}

Calculate the two partial derivatives separately.

:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="Solution"}

We obtain

$$
f_x=2x,\qquad f_y=4y,
$$

so

$$
\nabla f(x,y)=\langle 2x,4y\rangle.
$$

At $(1,2)$, this becomes

$$
\nabla f(1,2)=\langle 2,8\rangle.
$$

:::
